userStories.title: Add GitLab merge-request, tree and member reads
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend the existing access-based GitLab client with the read primitives required by all five consumer stories.

**Motivation** — After features 1 and 2, a GitLab repo can be registered and can run every job kind, but the features that read its code or its merge requests still check `provider === 'github'` or `githubInstallationId !== null` and stop.

**Approach** — GitLab client additions (design section 5):

`GitLabAccessChecker` (`apps/api/src/fleet/git-broker/gitlab-access-checker.ts`) gains four reads and one field.
Every new method calls `assertGitLabHostAllowed` before each request and maps 401 to `gitlab_token_invalid`, 403
to `app_permissions_insufficient`, and any other unexpected status to `provider_error`, through the existing
private `fail`.

| Method | Request | Answer |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `getMergeRequest` (existing) | unchanged | adds `headSha` when the body's `sha` is a string; leaves it absent otherwise |
| `getTree(access, ref)` | `GET <project>/repository/tree?ref=<ref>&recursive=true&per_page=100&page=<n>`, n = 1.. | `{ entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]; truncated: boolean }`, mapped as `listTree` maps them (`size: null`). Paging stops at the first page shorter than 100. When page `TREE_FULL_MAX_PAGES` (a static `= 100` beside `TREE_MAX_PAGES`) is full, the method stops and answers `truncated: true` with the entries read so far, including for a tree of exactly 10000 entries. A 404 on any page throws `repo_not_found`; a 200 whose body is not an array throws `provider_error`. |
| `listMergeRequestNotes(access, iid)` | `GET <project>/merge_requests/<iid>/notes?per_page=100` (one page) | the `body` strings of the notes, in response order; 404 throws `repo_not_found`; a 200 whose body is not an array throws `provider_error` |
| `getMergeRequestDiscussion(access, iid, discussionId)` | `GET <project>/merge_requests/<iid>/discussions/<encodeURIComponent(discussionId)>` | `{ authors: string[] }`, the `author.username` of each note that has one; 404 answers `null`; a 200 whose `notes` is not an array throws `provider_error` |
| `getMemberAccessLevel(access, username)` | `GET <project>/members/all?query=<encodeURIComponent(username)>&per_page=100` | the `access_level` of the entry whose `username` equals `username` case-insensitively; `0` when none matches; 404 throws `repo_not_found`; a 200 whose body is not an array throws `provider_error` |

`members/all` includes inherited group membership, so a group Developer counts as a Developer on the project.
The design names `members/all/:user_id`, but a review event carries only logins, so the lookup queries by
username and confirms the exact match itself (`query` matches fuzzily).

**Scope** — In: extend existing client and existing gitlab-access-checker.spec.ts; retain the 10-page listTree behavior and current MR state/mergeSha mapping; add no files. Out: US-002 project assignment/token fences; US-003 brief; US-004 indexing/polling; US-005 rulings; US-006 parser/minter. Paging MR notes past the first 100 in the rulings item-index check; a full page fails open, as on GitHub. US-006 only: paging `members/all` past the first 100 matches of the username query; an exact match beyond them counts as access level 0 (not a writer).

**Interface** — `getMergeRequest(access, iid)` adds optional `headSha` to existing `VcsPrStatus`; `getTree(access, ref)` answers `{ entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]; truncated: boolean }`; `listMergeRequestNotes(access, iid)` answers note body strings; `getMergeRequestDiscussion(access, iid, discussionId)` answers `{ authors: string[] }` or null; `getMemberAccessLevel(access, username)` answers numeric access level. Existing integration signatures: `GitLabAccessChecker.getBranchHead(access, branch): Promise<string>`, `getFile(access, path, ref): Promise<ForgeFile | null>`, `listTree(access, path, ref): Promise<ForgeTreeEntry[]>`, `GITLAB_DEVELOPER_ACCESS = 30`. Keep repo-host/numeric-project-id addressing through the existing GitLabAccess target; do not change credential resolution or GitHub clients.

**Verification** — Extend existing DNS/HTTP-stubbed unit suite with table-driven status, shape and host failures and exact paging/URL assertions; use strict three-session TDD because calls carry credentials and enforce outbound host security.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [unit] GitLabAccessChecker.getMergeRequest(access, 7) for a 200 body whose sha is 'abc123' returns an object with headSha: 'abc123', and for a body with no sha returns an object with no headSha property.

AC-2 [unit] getTree(access, 'h1') requests GET <apiBase>/projects/<projectId>/repository/tree?ref=h1&recursive=true&per_page=100&page=1, then page 2 when page 1 holds 100 entries, and stops after a page of fewer than 100, returning { entries, truncated: false } with the blob and tree entries of both pages mapped as { path, type, sha: id, size: null }.
AC-3 [unit] getTree when each of 100 pages holds 100 entries makes exactly 100 requests and returns truncated: true with the 10000 entries read.
AC-4 [unit] getTree throws RepoCheckException with reason repo_not_found when GitLab answers 404 to page 1, and also when page 1 holds 100 entries and page 2 answers 404.

AC-5 [unit] listMergeRequestNotes(access, 4) requests GET <apiBase>/projects/<projectId>/merge_requests/4/notes?per_page=100 and returns the body strings of the notes in response order, ignoring an entry whose body is not a string.
AC-6 [unit] listMergeRequestNotes throws RepoCheckException with reason provider_error for a 200 response whose body is an object instead of an array.

AC-7 [unit] getMergeRequestDiscussion(access, 4, 'd/1') requests GET <apiBase>/projects/<projectId>/merge_requests/4/discussions/d%2F1 and returns { authors: ['alice', 'bob'] } for a body whose notes carry authors alice and bob and one note with no author.
AC-8 [unit] getMergeRequestDiscussion returns null when GitLab answers 404.

AC-9 [unit] getMemberAccessLevel(access, 'Alice.B') requests GET <apiBase>/projects/<projectId>/members/all?query=Alice.B&per_page=100 and returns 30 when the response holds { username: 'alice.b', access_level: 30 } and { username: 'alice.bx', access_level: 50 }.
AC-10 [unit] getMemberAccessLevel returns 0 when no entry's username equals the queried username case-insensitively.

AC-11 [unit] Each of getTree, listMergeRequestNotes, getMergeRequestDiscussion and getMemberAccessLevel throws RepoCheckException with reason gitlab_token_invalid on 401, app_permissions_insufficient on 403 and provider_error on 500 (one table-driven test).

AC-12 [unit] Each of the four new methods, for an access whose api base host resolves to a loopback address, throws RepoCheckException with reason gitlab_host_blocked and sends no request (one table-driven test).

AC-13 [unit] getTree, listMergeRequestNotes and getMemberAccessLevel throw RepoCheckException with reason provider_error for a 200 whose body is an object instead of an array, getMergeRequestDiscussion throws it for a 200 whose notes is missing, and listMergeRequestNotes and getMemberAccessLevel throw repo_not_found on 404 (one table-driven test).

routing.reasoning: Bounded additive client operations reuse existing transport/types, but credential-bearing requests, SSRF guards and membership reads require security-isolated TDD.

userStories.title: Allow PROJECT threads to fetch connected GitLab repositories
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Make connected GitLab repos fetchable for PROJECT sessions and let the existing fenced sync mint return their read token.

**Motivation** — `project-repos-assign.ts` lists every GitLab repo as `not a GitHub repository`, so a PROJECT thread never reads GitLab code, and the token fence refuses its token request with `repo_not_assigned`.

**Approach** — Threads with project code:

`PrismaFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos` also selects `gitlabCredential: { select: { writeTokenUserId,
writeTokenUsername } }` and maps it to `gitlabWriteUser: { id, username }`, or `null` when there is no row. The
`gitlabCredential` relation is destructured out of the row first, so a returned `FleetRepoRef` carries
`gitlabWriteUser` and no `gitlabCredential` key (unlike `findRepo`, which spreads the raw row).
`fetchableProjectRepos` keeps a repo when it is GitHub with an installation, **or** GitLab with a truthy
`gitlabWriteUser`. `unavailableReason` answers `no installation` for a GitLab repo whose `gitlabWriteUser` is
null or absent, and null for one that has it. A ref built without the field (older fixtures and callers) is
therefore not connected. `withProjectRepos` already builds the clone URL with `cloneUrlFor`, which
uses a GitLab repo's own host.

The token fence in `SyncService` recomputes the fetchable list with the same `fetchableProjectRepos`, so a granted
GitLab repo reaches `GitTokenBroker.mint` with `readOnly: true`. Feature 2 already answers that mint with the
repo's **read** token, `username: 'oauth2'` and the `repoId`. This feature adds no broker code.

A GitLab repo is readable when it has a `FleetRepoGitlabCredential` row (feature 1). A repo without one is "not
connected". Thread project code reuses `ProjectRepoUnavailable.reason` `no installation` (owner ruling 2026-11-16: the reason list is closed in `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` and the runner's assign parser, so no new reason is added). Keep input order and the existing 10 fetchable/50 unavailable limits.

**Scope** — In: project-repo projection, pure assignment predicates and existing unit/integration specs; sync uses its existing shared predicate and fenced readOnly grant. Update project-repos-assign.spec.ts and placement.service.project-code.spec.ts GitLab-without-credential reasons from `not a GitHub repository` to `no installation`, retaining order/cap assertions. Add gitlabWriteUser and nested credential select to prisma-fleet-job.repository.find-project-repos.spec.ts expectations; add gitlabWriteUser:null to both whole-row expectations in fleet-project-code-repository.integration.spec.ts. In fleet-project-code-token-fence.integration.spec.ts keep pc-gitlab disconnected/refused, add a distinct connected GitLab repo, add VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY to ENV_KEYS and set it before app boot, and seed both differing tokens through GitLabRepoCredentials.save so they decrypt. Out: US-001 checker methods; US-003 brief; US-004 knowledge; US-005 rulings; US-006 reviews. A new `ProjectRepoUnavailable` reason for a GitLab repo without credentials; it reuses `no installation` so that `@nathapp/fleet-protocol` and the runner's assign parser do not change (owner ruling 2026-11-16). US-002 only: no test asserts token values are absent from log lines; `SyncService` and the broker log only job ids and error names.

**Interface** — `fetchableProjectRepos(repos)`; `PrismaFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos(projectId)` returns FleetRepoRef rows with `gitlabWriteUser: { id, username }` or null and no raw relation; `withProjectRepos(thread, repos, vcs)` retains ThreadAssign shape. Reuse `cloneUrlFor(repo, cfg)` and `GitTokenBroker.mint` GitLab `readOnly` branch from feature 2.

**Verification** — Extend existing assignment/projection unit suites and real PG+HTTP sync/repository suites, asserting exact stored read plaintext versus distinct write plaintext, oauth2, repoId and unchanged disconnected/foreign-project/REPO-thread fences. Run DB suites outside sandbox through scoped host command; strict three-session TDD for token authorization.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] PrismaFleetJobRepository.findProjectRepos(projectId) returns, for a GitLab repo with a FleetRepoGitlabCredential row whose write user is (7, 'kodabot'), gitlabWriteUser: { id: 7, username: 'kodabot' }, and gitlabWriteUser: null for a GitLab repo without a row.

AC-2 [unit] fetchableProjectRepos keeps, in input order, a GitHub repo with an installation and a GitLab repo with a non-null gitlabWriteUser, and drops a GitLab repo whose gitlabWriteUser is null, a GitLab repo with no gitlabWriteUser property, and a GitHub repo whose githubInstallationId is null.
AC-3 [unit] withProjectRepos lists a GitLab repo with a non-null gitlabWriteUser and host https://gitlab.example.com in projectRepos with cloneUrl https://gitlab.example.com/<owner>/<name>.git.
AC-4 [unit] withProjectRepos lists a GitLab repo whose gitlabWriteUser is null in projectReposUnavailable with reason no installation.
AC-5 [unit] withProjectRepos with 10 fetchable GitHub repos followed by one GitLab repo with a gitlabWriteUser lists the GitLab repo as unavailable with reason limit.

AC-6 [integration] A runner sync whose token request names a PROJECT SESSION job and a GitLab repo of its project that has a credential row is granted a git token with username: 'oauth2', repoId equal to that repo's id, and token equal to the stored read token's plaintext.
AC-7 [integration] The same sync never answers that request with the stored write token's plaintext: a repo whose read and write tokens differ yields the read token only.
AC-8 [integration] A runner sync whose token request names a GitLab repo of the project without a credential row answers a gitTokenErrors entry with reason repo_not_assigned for that repoId.

routing.reasoning: Two production files add a credential-presence projection and extend an existing predicate; sync and broker already consume that predicate, while session/token authorization still mandates strict isolated TDD.

modifiedFiles.reason: the cases that build GitLab repos with no `gitlabWriteUser` assert the reason `not a GitHub repository`; with this story such a repo is unavailable with reason `no installation`, and a GitLab repo with a `gitlabWriteUser` is fetchable. Replace each `not a GitHub repository` expectation with `no installation` and keep the order and cap assertions unchanged.

line 108 expects a GitLab repo with no credential to be unavailable with reason `not a GitHub repository`; with this story it is `no installation`. Replace that reason and keep the rest of the expectation unchanged.

the mapped-row `toEqual` (lines 43-46) and the exact `select` assertion (lines 59-66) pin the projection before this story; the row now also carries `gitlabWriteUser` (null for a repo without a credential row) and the select adds `gitlabCredential: { select: { writeTokenUserId: true, writeTokenUsername: true } }`. Add both to the expectations.

lines 78-83 `toEqual` whole rows from `findProjectRepos`; each row now also carries `gitlabWriteUser` (null for both rows there, since neither has a credential row). Add `gitlabWriteUser: null` to each expected row.

the `pc-gitlab` repo has no credential row and stays refused with `repo_not_assigned`; add a GitLab repo with a credential row whose request is granted. The suite sets only `GITHUB_*` and `FLEET_SYNC_WAIT_MS` today; add `VCS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` to `ENV_KEYS` and set it before the app boots, and seed the credential row through `GitLabRepoCredentials.save` so the stored tokens decrypt. The existing refusal assertion stays valid and must not be weakened.

userStories.title: Read project briefs from GitLab default branches
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add read-token GitLab repository context to the existing cached, bounded project brief service.

**Motivation** — `ProjectBriefService` answers `Repository context: unavailable (not a GitHub repository)`.

**Approach** — Project brief:

`ProjectBriefService.attempt` keeps its GitHub branch unchanged. A GitLab repo:

1. reads the head with `GitLabAccessChecker.getBranchHead(access, defaultBranch)`, then `.nax/context.md` and
   then `AGENTS.md` with `getFile(access, path, sha)`, each in its own `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)`;
2. answers `Repository context: unavailable (no credentials)` when that first `call` throws
   `gitlab_credentials_missing`. A cached entry inside its 300000 ms TTL is still served without any `call`, as
   on GitHub. After the TTL, `gitlab_credentials_missing` is the one failure that does not fall back to the
   cached text: the read's failure handling checks for it and answers `unavailable (no credentials)`, because
   the repo has lost its read access. Every other failure keeps the `, cached` fallback. There is no separate
   `resolve` before the reads;
3. shares the GitHub path's cache (keyed by repo id and checked against the head sha), the 3000 ms deadline, the
   masking and capping, and the `, cached` fallback.

`UnavailableReason` gains `no credentials`.

In every changed class, the GitLab branch is taken **if and only if `provider === 'gitlab'`**. A repo or ref
with any other provider, or with none (older fixtures), takes the GitHub path unchanged.

New constructor dependencies are appended after the existing required ones, in this order:
`GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`.

- `ProjectBriefService(github, repos, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker, @Optional() now?)`

An existing spec that builds one of these positionally without the new arguments keeps working on its GitHub
cases.

Every GitLab read goes through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)`, **one `call` per forge request**,
never one `call` wrapped around a whole pass or a sequence of requests. A `fn` lets every `RepoCheckException`
propagate out of `call`, and the caller degrades outside it. So a 401 marks the read token invalid (feature 1
behaviour) even where the feature then degrades, and a token rotated in the middle of a long knowledge pass is
never marked invalid by a refusal of the old one. No read ever passes `'write'` to `call` or `resolve`.

**Scope** — In: service GitLab branch and existing service tests; shared repo-id/head cache, masking, cap and deadline. Replace the obsolete GitLab no-context table reason with no credentials and a missing-row store fixture in project-brief.service.spec.ts; shift its positional clock after the two new dependencies. Out: US-001 client additions, US-002 assignment/token fence, US-004 knowledge indexing, US-005 rulings and US-006 review minting.

**Interface** — `ProjectBriefService(github, repos, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker, @Optional() now?)`; `resolveRepoContext(repoId)` retains its never-throwing section-string interface. Use `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` only with 'read'; `GitLabAccessChecker.getBranchHead(access, branch): Promise<string>` and `getFile(access, path, ref): Promise<ForgeFile | null>`.

**Verification** — Extend project-brief.service.spec.ts using fake time, distinct accesses supplied to each callback, missing-row and failed/timeout reads, no GitHub calls for GitLab, and exact unchanged GitHub argument assertions. A real credential-store unit collaborator or faithful wrapper must demonstrate 401 invalidation occurs before cached degradation; do not catch inside fn. Strict three-session TDD because credential selection and cached access removal are security-sensitive.
acceptanceCriteria:
AC-1 [unit] ProjectBriefService.resolveRepoContext(repoId) for a GitLab repo with credentials, whose getBranchHead answers 'abcdef1234' and whose getFile answers .nax/context.md with text 'hello', returns exactly 'Repository context (<owner>/<name> .nax/context.md @ abcdef1):
hello' (with one newline before hello and no trailing period).

AC-2 [unit] For that repo the head is read with GitLabAccessChecker.getBranchHead on the repo's default branch and the file with getFile(access, '.nax/context.md', 'abcdef1234'), each called with the access a separate GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn) passes to fn. call is never invoked with 'write', and no GitHubAppClient method is called.
AC-3 [unit] For a GitLab repo whose .nax/context.md is absent and whose AGENTS.md holds agents, resolveRepoContext returns the AGENTS.md section.

AC-4 [unit] For a GitLab repo whose first GitLabRepoCredentials.call throws RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing'), resolveRepoContext returns Repository context: unavailable (no credentials) and calls no GitLabAccessChecker method.
AC-5 [unit] A second resolveRepoContext for the same GitLab repo within 300000 ms returns the cached section and calls getBranchHead only once in total.

AC-6 [unit] For a GitLab repo with a cached entry, a resolveRepoContext after the 300000 ms TTL whose first GitLabRepoCredentials.call throws RepoCheckException('gitlab_credentials_missing') returns Repository context: unavailable (no credentials), not the cached text.

AC-7 [unit] For a GitLab repo whose cached entry exists and whose next getBranchHead throws RepoCheckException('gitlab_token_invalid') after the TTL, resolveRepoContext returns the cached text marked ', cached'.
AC-8 [unit] For a GitLab repo with no cached entry and a getFile that throws, resolveRepoContext returns Repository context: unavailable (read failed).

AC-9 [unit] For a GitHub repo, resolveRepoContext calls GitHubAppClient.mintInstallationToken, getBranchHead and getFile with the same arguments as before and never calls GitLabRepoCredentials.resolve or call.

AC-10 [unit; failure handling] Given a connected GitLab repo without cached text, when its brief forge read answers 401 inside GitLabRepoCredentials.call, GitLabRepoCredentials.markInvalid(repo.id, 'read') is called before resolveRepoContext returns 'Repository context: unavailable (read failed)', preserving the existing read-failed degradation.

AC-11 [unit; failure handling] Given a GitLab brief cache entry older than the 300000 ms TTL, when the next brief read exceeds the 3000 ms deadline, resolveRepoContext returns that cached text marked ', cached'.
AC-12 [unit; failure handling] When a GitLab brief read exceeds the 3000 ms deadline and no cached text exists, resolveRepoContext returns Repository context: unavailable (timeout).

routing.reasoning: Existing service/cache patterns localize the change, but read credentials, invalidation and stale-cache behavior after access removal require security-isolated TDD.

modifiedFiles.reason: the table case "a GitLab repository" expects `not a GitHub repository`; with this story a GitLab repo with no credential row answers `unavailable (no credentials)`. Replace that row's reason and give its fixture a credential store that has no row for the repo. Its `new ProjectBriefService(github, repos, clock)` constructions also gain the two GitLab dependencies, placed before the optional clock.

userStories.title: Index and poll connected GitLab repository knowledge
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend repository projections, polling and the existing leased Markdown indexing pass to connected GitLab repos using per-request read access.

**Motivation** — `KnowledgeRepoIndexer` records every GitLab repo `skipped` with `not a GitHub repository`, and the poller reads only GitHub repos.

**Approach** — Knowledge index:

- `KnowledgeRepoRef` gains `host?: string` and `gitlabConnected?: boolean` (absent counts as not connected, so
  refs built without it stay valid). `REPO_SELECT` adds `host` and
  `gitlabCredential: { select: { repoId: true } }`. `toRepo` sets `gitlabConnected` to whether that relation is
  non-null, and does not copy the relation itself onto the ref.
- `IKnowledgeIndexRepository` gains `findAllGitlabRepos(): Promise<KnowledgeRepoRef[]>`: GitLab repos that have a
  credential row, ordered `createdAt` then `id`, at most 500. `findAllGithubRepos` is unchanged.
- `KnowledgePoller.poll` enqueues the repos from `findAllGithubRepos` and then from `findAllGitlabRepos`, each
  with reason `'poll'`. Each read has its own `try`, so a failure of one source still enqueues the other's repos
  and logs one warning.
- `KnowledgeRepoIndexer.indexRepo`, for a GitLab repo:
  - without `gitlabConnected`, it records `skipped` with `lastError` `no credentials` and claims nothing;
  - otherwise it runs the same pass as GitHub, with one `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)` per forge
    request: `getBranchHead` for the head, `getTree(access, head)` for the tree (`truncated` fails the pass with
    `tree truncated`, as on GitHub), and `getFile(access, path, head)` for each kept file;
  - a GitLab tree entry has `size: null`, so the allowlist cannot skip a large file before it is fetched. A
    fetched file whose `ForgeFile.size` is above `MAX_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_BYTES` is therefore counted in
    `skippedCount`, and any earlier rows for its path are deleted as the GitHub missing-file branch deletes
    them: `store.deleteFile(projectId, 'repo:<repoId>:<path>')`, then `state.deleteFile(repoId, path)`. It is not
    chunked. The GitLab files API returns the whole body, so the file is read into memory before the skip.
- The provider check moves: a GitHub repo with no installation still records `no installation`, and the
  `not a GitHub repository` reason goes away.

In every changed class, the GitLab branch is taken **if and only if `provider === 'gitlab'`**. A repo or ref
with any other provider, or with none (older fixtures), takes the GitHub path unchanged.

New constructor dependencies are appended after the existing required ones, in this order:
`GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`.

- `KnowledgeRepoIndexer(state, github, store, embeddings, rag, audit, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker, clock = Date.now)`

An existing spec that builds one of these positionally without the new arguments keeps working on its GitHub
cases.

Every GitLab read goes through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)`, **one `call` per forge request**,
never one `call` wrapped around a whole pass or a sequence of requests. A `fn` lets every `RepoCheckException`
propagate out of `call`, and the caller degrades outside it. So a 401 marks the read token invalid (feature 1
behaviour) even where the feature then degrades, and a token rotated in the middle of a long knowledge pass is
never marked invalid by a refusal of the old one. No read ever passes `'write'` to `call` or `resolve`.

**Scope** — In: knowledge-index.domain.ts, prisma-knowledge-index.repository.ts, knowledge-poller.ts, knowledge-repo-indexer.ts and existing specs. Preserve claim/renew fencing, serial file commits, unchanged-head/pattern-key/unembedded logic, embeddings/chunks, audit, optimization and outcome indexing. In knowledge-repo-indexer.spec.ts change AC-9's GitLab row and the older GitLab refusal test to gitlabConnected:false/no credentials, keep GitHub no installation unchanged, and put both new dependencies before defaulted clock in every affected construction. In knowledge-poller.spec.ts give all repository stubs findAllGitlabRepos returning [] so old GitHub enqueue assertions retain meaning. Extend prisma-knowledge-index.repository.spec.ts and the existing PG repository block in test/integration/fleet/knowledge-store.integration.spec.ts for projections and enumeration. Out: US-001 getTree/client implementation, US-002 assignment, US-003 briefs, US-005 rulings, US-006 review decisions. US-004 only: retrying a GitLab call inside a knowledge pass; a failed call fails the pass, and the next poll or merge event runs it again. US-004 only: the GitHub tree cap and the GitHub pass are unchanged; only the GitLab pass reads `getTree`. US-004 only: a GitLab repo whose recursive tree holds more than 10000 entries always fails its pass with `tree truncated`; a narrower tree read is a later change. US-004 only: a GitLab file skipped after fetch for its size keeps no `KnowledgeRepoFile` row, so it is fetched again on the next pass that sees a new head; a skip marker is a later change.

**Interface** — `host?: string`; `gitlabConnected?: boolean`; `findAllGitlabRepos(): Promise<KnowledgeRepoRef[]>`; `KnowledgeRepoIndexer(state, github, store, embeddings, rag, audit, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker, clock = Date.now)`. Reuse `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` with 'read', `GitLabAccessChecker.getBranchHead(access, branch): Promise<string>`, `getTree(access, ref)` answering `{ entries: ForgeTreeEntry[]; truncated: boolean }`, and `getFile(access, path, ref): Promise<ForgeFile | null>`. `MAX_KNOWLEDGE_FILE_BYTES = 262_144`.

**Verification** — Existing Vitest indexer/poller tests use injected state, store, embeddings, forge and clock; assert separately supplied read accesses for head/tree/every file, no GitHub methods, deletion order/count for oversized GitLab files, unchanged passes, source failure isolation and exact reason propagation. PG tests prove relation presence, host and stable ordered enumeration; run host scoped command rather than treating sandbox skips as verification. Strict three-session TDD for credential isolation across a long pass.
acceptanceCriteria: AC-1 [integration] PrismaKnowledgeIndexRepository.findRepo(id) returns gitlabConnected: true and the repo's host for a GitLab repo with a credential row, and gitlabConnected: false for a GitLab repo without one.
AC-2 [integration] findAllGitlabRepos() returns the GitLab repos with a credential row, ordered by createdAt then id, and omits GitLab repos without a row and every GitHub repo.
AC-3 [unit] KnowledgePoller.poll() enqueues every repo id from findAllGithubRepos and then every repo id from findAllGitlabRepos, each with reason 'poll'.

AC-4 [unit] KnowledgePoller.poll() when findAllGithubRepos rejects still enqueues every repo id from findAllGitlabRepos, when findAllGitlabRepos rejects still enqueues every repo id from findAllGithubRepos, and in both cases resolves without throwing.

userStories.title: Support rulings and FIX snapshots for GitLab merge requests
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Admit draft GitLab MR RUN targets, read their item indexes and attach pending rulings to FIX snapshots with the read credential.

**Motivation** — `PrismaFleetPrRulingRepository` computes no PR number for a GitLab job, so `POST .../rulings` answers 409 "Only draft RUN jobs with a GitHub pull request can be ruled"; `snapshotForFix` answers `notSent: 'head-unreadable'` for every GitLab FIX.

**Approach** — PR rulings:

- `RulingTargetRepo` gains `id: string` and `host?: string`; `targetRepo` copies them from the job's repo row.
- `PrismaFleetPrRulingRepository.lockTarget` and `findTarget` compute `prNumber` with
  `prNumberFor(job.repo, job.resultPrUrl)` for both providers. `prNumberFor` already parses a GitLab MR URL,
  including a host path prefix.
- `latestRunForPr` and `runsForPr` accept a GitLab repo. `latestRunForPr`'s pre-filter is
  `resultPrUrl: { endsWith: '/merge_requests/<n>' }` for GitLab (it stays `/pull/<n>` for GitHub), and every match
  is still confirmed with `prNumberFor`.
- `replaceOlderRuns` accepts a GitLab RUN.
- `FleetPrRulingsService.snapshotForFix`, for a GitLab repo, reads the MR with
  `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', a => GitLabAccessChecker.getMergeRequest(a, prNumber))`:
  - `null`, or a state other than `open`, answers `notSent: 'pr-not-open'`;
  - a missing `headSha` or any thrown error answers `notSent: 'head-unreadable'`;
  - otherwise it answers the same `{ headSha, rulings }` as GitHub.
- `assertItemIndex`, for a GitLab repo, reads `listMergeRequestNotes` through `call(repo, 'read', fn)`. It applies
  the GitHub rules: fail open on any error and on a full page of 100, and refuse with `fleet.rulings.noItemIndex`
  when no note body contains `NAX_ITEM_INDEX_MARKER`.
- The `fleet.rulings.notDraft` message drops "GitHub":
  - en: "Only draft RUN jobs with a pull or merge request can be ruled";
  - zh: "只能裁定具有拉取请求或合并请求的草稿 RUN 作业".
- The `fleet.rulings.invalidPr` message drops "GitHub" too:
  - en: "The job must identify a pull or merge request";
  - zh: "任务必须指定拉取请求或合并请求".

In every changed class, the GitLab branch is taken **if and only if `provider === 'gitlab'`**. A repo or ref
with any other provider, or with none (older fixtures), takes the GitHub path unchanged.

New constructor dependencies are appended after the existing required ones, in this order:
`GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`.

- `FleetPrRulingsService(repo, txManager, audit, ticketEffects, github, actors, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker)`

An existing spec that builds one of these positionally without the new arguments keeps working on its GitHub
cases.

Every GitLab read goes through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)`, **one `call` per forge request**,
never one `call` wrapped around a whole pass or a sequence of requests. A `fn` lets every `RepoCheckException`
propagate out of `call`, and the caller degrades outside it. So a 401 marks the read token invalid (feature 1
behaviour) even where the feature then degrades, and a token rotated in the middle of a long knowledge pass is
never marked invalid by a refusal of the old one. No read ever passes `'write'` to `call` or `resolve`.

**Scope** — In: target id/host projection, MR attribution/newest/every-RUN lookup, older pending replacement, read-token snapshot/notes checks, and both en/zh message pairs. Keep eligibility/approval ordering, pending snapshot ordering/cap and repo-first transaction locks. In fleet-pr-rulings.integration.spec.ts remove gitlab only from AC-2 refused kinds, update checked notDraft text and add accepted GitLab draft RUN. In fleet-pr-rulings.preflight.spec.ts replace GitLab no-read case with missing-row fail-open and no GitHub method; extend existing snapshot/service/repository/integration specs without new files. Out: US-001 checker methods, US-002 project fetch, US-003 brief, US-004 index, US-006 review minter. Paging MR notes past the first 100 in the rulings item-index check; a full page fails open, as on GitHub. US-005 only: concurrent rulings on one GitLab MR; the existing repo-first row locks of `lockTarget` apply unchanged. Flows, auto-review, fix-checks (`trustDetectedChecks`), CI pipeline status and host-aware `findByIdentity` on GitLab (feature 4 of GitLab parity); their GitHub-only guards stay.

**Interface** — `RulingTargetRepo` gains `id: string` and `host?: string`; `FleetPrRulingsService(repo, txManager, audit, ticketEffects, github, actors, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker)`; reuse `prNumberFor(repo: Pick<FleetRepoRef, 'provider' | 'owner' | 'name' | 'host'>, url): number | null`. Read through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` with 'read', `getMergeRequest(access, iid)` and `listMergeRequestNotes(access, iid)`. Reuse `NAX_ITEM_INDEX_MARKER` from fleet-pr-rulings.service.ts.

**Verification** — Existing PG+HTTP suite proves MR number/host projection, newest 12 versus 112, all runs, replacement and REST 201/409 eligibility. Existing preflight/snapshot unit suites assert separate supplied read access, fail-open notes and closed/missing-head/error snapshots, and unchanged GitHub thread-read calls. Validate 401 read-token marking before graceful degradation. Use scoped host DB execution and strict three-session TDD for credentials and ruling eligibility.

userStories.title: Mint review decisions from GitLab merge-request disagreements
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Accept GitLab usernames and verify GitLab Developer writers/discussion authors before minting provider-attributed review decisions.

**Motivation** — `ReviewEventMinter` skips every GitLab review event as `repo-unavailable`, and the bot-review parser drops a GitLab username that carries a `.` or `_`.

**Approach** — Review events:

- The bot-review parser's `LOGIN` accepts either the GitHub login pattern (unchanged) or a GitLab username:
  `^[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]{0,254}$`.
- `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo` adds `provider` and `host` to its projection.
- `ReviewEventMinter.mintOne` keeps its order: the bot-only skip, then `writer.guard`, then `findReviewRepo`.
  Only after `findReviewRepo` is the provider known. Then, for a GitHub repo:
  - it drops every login that does not match the GitHub login pattern, skipping the row `no-writer` when none is
    left;
  - then runs exactly as today. A GitHub event whose logins pass the old pattern makes the same calls.
- For a GitLab repo, each forge request runs in its own `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)`:
  - `writers` keeps each login whose `getMemberAccessLevel` is at least `GITLAB_DEVELOPER_ACCESS` (30) (owner
    ruling 2026-11-16);
  - `verifiedWriter` reads `getMergeRequestDiscussion(access, row.prNumber, row.threadId)`. `null` or a thrown
    error is unverified. Otherwise the first writer, in `writers` order, whose login equals a thread author
    case-insensitively (`normalizeLogin`, as on GitHub) is verified;
  - the approver id is `gitlab:<login>`;
  - the access-level lookups decide the row's failure path from the `RepoCheckException` reason `call` throws:
    - `gitlab_credentials_missing` skips the row as `repo-unavailable`, as a GitHub repo with no installation
      does, because a disconnected repo does not heal on retry;
    - `vcs_encryption_key_missing` takes the existing `retry` path (`bumpAttempt`, then `mint-failed` after 3);
    - any other failure, `gitlab_token_invalid` included, skips the row as `permission-check-failed`, as on
      GitHub. Its `call` has already marked the read token invalid.
- The `[bot]` filter stays. On GitLab, nax already drops its own login from `disagreedBy` (nax
  `bot/post-earlier.ts` `withdrawalEvents`).

In every changed class, the GitLab branch is taken **if and only if `provider === 'gitlab'`**. A repo or ref
with any other provider, or with none (older fixtures), takes the GitHub path unchanged.

New constructor dependencies are appended after the existing required ones, in this order:
`GitLabRepoCredentials`, then `GitLabAccessChecker`.

- `ReviewEventMinter(events, repos, github, writer, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker)`

An existing spec that builds one of these positionally without the new arguments keeps working on its GitHub
cases.

Every GitLab read goes through `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo, 'read', fn)`, **one `call` per forge request**,
never one `call` wrapped around a whole pass or a sequence of requests. A `fn` lets every `RepoCheckException`
propagate out of `call`, and the caller degrades outside it. So a 401 marks the read token invalid (feature 1
behaviour) even where the feature then degrades, and a token rotated in the middle of a long knowledge pass is
never marked invalid by a refusal of the old one. No read ever passes `'write'` to `call` or `resolve`.

**Scope** — In: bot-review parser union login validation, safe review repo projection and provider-specific writer/thread verification in the existing minter. Keep writer.guard, bot-only skip, review approval context, idempotent writer/bookkeeping and retry paths in their existing order. Update fleet-repos.service.spec.ts exact review projection to include provider/host; make existing review-event.minter.spec.ts repo fixtures explicitly provider:'github' so their original assertions keep meaning. Extend existing bot-review.parser.spec.ts and minter specs with the GitLab access/discussion paths and provider-regression cases, no new files. Out: US-001 membership/discussion client implementation, US-002 project code, US-003 brief, US-004 index and US-005 rulings. Excluding the write token's username from a GitLab review event's `disagreedBy` in koda; nax already drops its own login. US-006 only: paging `members/all` past the first 100 matches of the username query; an exact match beyond them counts as access level 0 (not a writer).

**Interface** — `ReviewEventMinter(events, repos, github, writer, gitlabCredentials, gitlabChecker)`; `FleetReposService.findReviewRepo(id)` adds provider and host to `{ id, projectId, owner, name, githubInstallationId, defaultBranch }`. Consume `getMemberAccessLevel(access, username)`, `getMergeRequestDiscussion(access, iid, discussionId)` returning `{ authors: string[] }` or null and `GITLAB_DEVELOPER_ACCESS = 30`. Each call uses `GitLabRepoCredentials.call(repo: { id: string; host?: string }, kind: 'read' | 'write', fn: (access: GitLabAccess) => Promise<T>): Promise<T>` with 'read'.

**Verification** — Existing minter harness asserts currentContext approval and bookkeeping. Extend it for separate read accesses, at-least-30 membership, writers order and case-insensitive discussion authors, verified/unverified approvals, three distinct access refusal paths, and unchanged GitHub role/thread calls after old-pattern filtering. Use the credential-store call seam to verify read invalidation on 401 rather than just mocking a thrown checker error.
